div.head: VIII Atr 27
div.ab: Gif mæssepreost ahwar stande on leasre gewitnesse oððe on mǽnan aðe oððe þeofa gewita ⁊ geweorhta beo, þonne sy he aworpen of gehadodra gemanan ⁊ þolige ægðer ge geferscipes ge freondscipes ge æghwilces wurðscipes, buton he wið God ⁊ wið men þe deoplicor gebete, fullice swa biscop him tæce, ⁊ him borh finde, þæt he þanan forð æfre swilces geswice.

Gif mæssepreost ahwar stande on leasre gewitnesse oððe on mǽnan aðe, oððe þeofa gewita ⁊ geweorhta beo, þonne sy he aworpen of gehadodra gemanan ⁊ þolige ægðer ge geferscipes ge freondscipes ge æghwilces wurðscipes, buton he wið God ⁊ wið men þe deoplicor gebete, fullice swa biscop him tæce, ⁊ him borh finde þæt he þanan forð æfre swilces geswice.

Gif mæssepreost ahwar stande on leasre gewitnesse oððe on mænan aðe oððe þeofa gewita and geweorhta beo, þonne sy he aworpen of gehadodra gemanan and þolige ægðer ge geferscipes, ge freondscipes, ge æghwilces wurðscipes, buton he wið God and wið men þe deoplicor gebete fullice swa biscop him tæce, and him borh finde, þæt he þanan forð æfre swilces geswice.

Wenn ein Priester irgendwo in falschem Zeugniss oder im Meineid [ertappt] dasteht, oder Mitwisser von Dieben und Mitwirker ist, dann sei er verstossen aus Gemeinschaft der Geistlichen und verliere sowohl [deren] Genossenschaft wie Freundschaft und jeden Ehrenrang, ausser wenn er gegenüber Gott und Weltlichen um so tiefer büsst — vollständig, wie [sein] Bischof ihm vorschreibt — und Bürgschaft für sich findet [dafür], dass er stets hinfort von solchem [Verbrechen] ablasse.

If a priest anywhere stands [convicted] of false witness or perjury, or is an accessory and accomplice of thieves, then let him be cast out of the fellowship of the clergy and lose both [their] fellowship and friendship and every honour, unless he makes all the deeper amends before God and men — in full, as [his] bishop prescribes for him — and finds surety [to the effect] that he will forever desist from such [crimes].

If a priest anywhere be concerned in false witness or perjury, or be the accessory and accomplice of thieves, he shall be cast out from the fellowship of those in holy orders, and shall forfeit both their society and their friendship and every kind of privilege, unless he make full amends, both towards God and towards men, to the utmost of his ability, as the bishop shall prescribe for him, and find surety that henceforth he will cease for ever from all such [wrong-doing].

If anywhere a mass-priest takes part in false witness or perjury, or is the accessory and accomplice of thieves, he is then to be cast out from the fellowship of those in orders, and to forfeit both the society and friendship and every dignity, unless he atone for it deeply towards God and towards men, in full as the bishop instructs him, and find for himself surety that he will from that time forth ever desist from such things.

If a priest is anywhere guilty of bearing false witness or committing perjury or being the aide or accomplice to thieves, then he is to be expelled from holy orders and deprived of companionship, friendship, and all entitlements unless he repents most deeply to God and the community entirely as the bishop instructs, and finds surety that he thenceforth will cease all wrongdoing.

note.seg: Einschliesslich Eideshilfe zu Falscheid; In Cn. Vgl. Gl Zeuge 5; Meineid 4. 6 [Ämterverlust setzt das Festland als Strafe; Böhmer Ki. u. Staat 81; dem Laien droht Leibesstrafe II Cn 36]; Geistliches Gericht 9c

Including oath-helping to a false oath; In Cn. Cf. Gl Zeuge 5; Meineid 4. 6 [on the Continent loss of office is laid down as the penalty; Böhmer Ki. u. Staat 81; the layman is threatened with corporal punishment II Cn 36]; Geistliches Gericht 9c
Vgl. Gl Mitwissen Z. 1, n. 1; vgl. o. 23 Anstiftung; Bürgschaft 6e
Cf. Gl Mitwissen l. 1, n. 1; cf. above 23 Anstiftung; Bürgschaft 6e
So Toller s. v. geferscipe; auch societate ordinatorum In Cn; aber s. o. 19¹. Besass der Priester die Würde des Thegn (s. d. Gl 10), so verliert er sie; s. u. 28f.
So Toller s. v. geferscipe; also societate ordinatorum In Cn; but see above 19¹. If the priest possessed the rank of thegn (see that word in Gl 10), he loses it; see below 28f.

Liebermann points out that, in the laws which show strong ecclesiastical influence, perjury is always regarded as one of the worst crimes, and is classed with murder and sorcery, cf. E. and G. 11; I Edm. 6; V Atr. 24 f.; VI, 7; 28, 2; 36; II Cn. 6.
